spots.name: Grand Mosque of Bursa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grand Mosque of Bursa is a historic mosque in Bursa, Turkey. It was commissioned by the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I to commemorate his great victory at the Battle of Nicopolis and built between 1396 and 1399.

spots.name: Green Mosque, Bursa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Green Mosque, also known as the Mosque of Mehmed I, is a part of a larger complex in eastern Bursa, Turkey, the former capital of the Ottoman Turks before Constantinople was captured in 1453. The complex consists of a mosque, a mausoleum known as the Green Tomb, a madrasa, a public kitchen, and a bathhouse.

spots.name: Cumalıkızık
spots.summary: Cumalıkızık is a neighbourhood in the municipality and district of Yıldırım, Bursa Province in Turkey. Its population is 707 (2022). It is 10 kilometers east of the city of Bursa, at the foot of Mount Uludağ. The village is now included within the border of the Yıldırım district as a neighbourhood.

spots.name: Muradiye Complex
spots.summary: The Muradiye Complex or the Complex of Sultan Murad II, the Ottoman sultan, is located in Bursa, Turkey. It is part of the historic UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Green Tomb
spots.summary: The Green Tomb is a mausoleum of the fifth Ottoman Sultan, Mehmed I, in Bursa, Turkey. It was built by Mehmed's son and successor Murad II following the death of the sovereign in 1421. The architect Hacı Ivaz Pasha designed the tomb and the Yeşil Mosque opposite to it.

spots.name: Emir Sultan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Emir Sultan Mosque is a mosque in Bursa, Turkey. First built in the 15th century, it was rebuilt in 1804 for the Ottoman sultan Selim III and rebuilt again in 1868, the plan of the mosque changing slightly with each rebuild.

spots.name: Bayezid I Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bayezid I Mosque is a historic mosque in Bursa, Turkey, that is part of the large complex (külliye) built by the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I between 1391–1395. It is situated in Bursa metropolitan district of Yıldırım, also named after the same sultan. It underwent extensive renovation following the 1855 Bursa earthquake.

spots.name: Koza Han
spots.summary: The Koza Han is a historic caravanserai (han) in Bursa, Turkey. It is located in the heart of the city's historic market district.

spots.name: Haji Özbek Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Haji Özbek Mosque is a historical Ottoman mosque in İznik, Turkey.

spots.name: Irgandı Bridge
spots.summary: Irgandı Bridge is a historical bridge in Bursa, Turkey. The bridge is over Gökdere, a tributary of Nilüfer River. It is between Osmangazi (northwest) and Yıldırım (southeast), two second level municipalities of Greater Bursa. The bridge is the only bazaar-bridge that was built in the Ottoman Empire.

spots.name: Tophane Clock Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Tophane Clock Tower is a clock tower in Bursa, Turkey. It has six floors and is 33m in height. The tower currently has a radio clock and is used as a fire lookout station.

spots.name: Orhan Gazi Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Orhan Gazi Mosque is a historic mosque in Bursa, Turkey. It is named after the Ottoman ruler Orhan, who founded the mosque in 1339–40 as part of a larger charitable complex. It is one of the oldest surviving monuments commissioned by the Ottoman dynasty.

spots.name: Prusa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Prusa or Prousa, or Prusa near Olympus or Prusa under Olympus, was an ancient Greek city located between Bithynia and Mysia, situated at the northern foot of the Mysian Olympus. Its site is occupied by the modern city of Bursa.

spots.name: Amir Sultan Cemetery
spots.summary: Amir Sultan Cemetery is a historical cemetery located in Yıldırım district of Bursa. The cemetery is named after the Islamic philosopher Amir Sultan.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Veled-i Yaniç Mosque is an Ottoman mosque with the type of early Ottoman architecture. The mosque is located in Bursa, Turkey and it is still in use. According to the inscription, which is above the entering door, it is known that this mosque was built at the July 1440 by Mahmud Çelebi.

spots.name: Beyazid I Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bayezid I built this religious complex in the 1390s, with mosque and madrassah. Crushed by Timur, he died in captivity in 1403 and eventually was buried in a cloistered tomb within the complex. By him lie his wife and son Isa.

spots.name: Ulu Hünkar Köşkü

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Make sure you walk all the way to the back of the garden, where a few tables offer a magnificent view over the bazaars below from the top of the old city wall. The Iskender kebap here is as good as the original. They also serve Turkish breakfast.

spots.name: Kitap Evi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For a still moderately priced splurge, go here. By arrangement, you can have your reserved table covered in rose petals, making it the perfect place for a marriage proposal. It's also a top class hotel.

spots.name: İskender Tarihi Ahşap Dükkan
spots.summary: This is the original of what's become a chain: İskender Efendi invented his style of kebab in Bursa in the 19th century.

spots.name: Çiçek Izgara
spots.summary: A grill restaurant beloved by locals and best known for its meatballs, has been around forever.
